points: We also had Deborah, a prophetess, a female prophet, a woman that God dealt with.

note.label: 7 WOMAN SHALL TAKE HOLD OF ONE MAN

points: Deborah, a prophetess: the Lord did deal with a woman on some level as a prophetess. They could refer to her as a prophetess because the woman was in order. Not because she doing what she want to do and giving her own sermon, but because she was in subjection to the men of Israel, the leaders of Israel.

Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, judged Israel at that time, dwelling under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: what kind of spirit was this king rolling in? He's asking a woman, Deborah, to roll with him to battle. That's a weak spirit. This is why the Lord revealed the mission or the vision to Deborah, cuz she was the only one that was obedient and had a spirit of order according to the scriptures. And the men at the time was weak.

If thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go: that's a weak brother. If Deborah was not rolling with the brother to battle or to counsel or to war, he would not go. That's why the Lord had to deal with Deborah. He couldn't find a brother that was fearless to do the mission, to do the work.

Barak answers, if thou wilt go with me, then I will go, but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go. Deborah agrees to go, but tells him the journey shall not be for his honour, for the Most High shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.

Now some sisters might take this and say, you see? The Lord do lead the woman to lead the man. I know you Christians. You might say, oh, see? You can have a prophetess and a teacher to lead Israel. Okay, well, let's see what kind of spirit Deborah was rolling in.

Sisera gathers all nine hundred chariots of iron unto the river of Kishon, and Deborah says unto Barak, up, for this is the day in which the Lord hath delivered Sisera into thine hand; is not the Lord gone out before thee?
See who's speaking here. Deborah's talking about she arose, a mother in Israel.

This passage is for all the closet feminists who think Deborah justifies women leading men. She did not lead men into any kind of war; she did not put on body armor and a breastplate, rise up on a horse, and lead the charge. She was the motivating factor to men that were shaky and fearful during that time, a mother in Israel, a guiding light.
